title: Efficacy and safety of RAD001 in advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC) patients (pts) progressing after first-line chemotherapy: A phase II study.

sections.abstract: e14500 Background: RAD001 (everolimus) is a derivate of rapamycin which acts as a signal transduction inhibitor. Its target is mTOR, a key protein kinase which regulates growth, proliferation and cell survival. Therapeutic effect of mTOR inhibitors on BTC has been evaluated in transgenic mouse models. RAD001 has recently been extensively evaluated in different cancer types. The aim of this study is to assess the disease control rate (DCR) defined as the proportion of patients with CR, PR or SD as a measure of the antitumor effect of RAD001 in cases with BTC progressing after first line chemotherapy. Methods: Eligibility criteria included unresectable or metastatic measurable biliary tract cancer (BTC)/gallbladder cancer (GBC), ECOG PS ≤ 2, adequate organ function and absence of clinically significant cardiovascular disease. It is planned to enroll a total of 37 pts, from 8 Centres. Patients receive oral RAD001 (10 mg daily dose) continuously from day 1 until progression or discontinuation for any cause. Radiological assessments are performed every 8 weeks. The data presented in the abstract refer subjects only from our Institution. Since February 2009, 18 pts (16 BTC; 2GBC) were enrolled and all are available for efficacy and safety. Median age was 60 years (range 42-75), male/female = 7/11, ECOG 0/1/2 = 7/8/3. Treatment related grade 3/4 toxicities included (number of pts): anemia (2), thrombocytopenia (4), transient SGPT/SGOT elevation (1), fatigue (2). No reactivation of HBV and HCV was observed during the treatment. The DCR was documented in 10 pts (55.5%):1 CR lasted for 9 months, 9 minor responses/SD with a median duration more than six months, and four cases are still in treatment. In 8 pts (44.5%) disease progressed. This preliminary analysis suggests that RAD001 can be safety administrated in chemotreated pts. The achievement of long lasting disease control and antitumor activity is encouraging, but more data needs to be further confirmed after the study is complete with a new trial employing RAD001 as front line therapy. Biological immunohistochemical expression of mTOR in pathological specimens is in progress. No significant financial relationships to disclose.
